text: "My business is property management. I manage my own houses and apartments. I have always worked out at a gym. This year I canceled my gym membership due to my loving Boot Camp so much. I work out at Boot Camp 5 days a week. My doctor's were so happy when I showed them results of my bone density test. My bone density was above average for my age. As we get older we lose muscle mass and that is why older people fall and break their bones much easier than a person who works out. I am 65 years young and besides having great bone density results from Boot Camp I am also more defined in area's where people my age have a lot of fat. Of course you also have to watch what you eat and Curtis has a great fat loss plan for you to follow and the fat does come off. In the past I have worked with four different trainers. As you know I am a cancer survivor or 6 Years now. I am a fighter and I give my all in everything in life. I appreciate so much more in life now and am grateful for everyday! I have to thank you for that changes that have taken place in my body. I have taken off more than 8 inches off my arms, hips, legs, and waist. I am so thankful Curtis did what four other trainers never did. This happened due to his dedication and love of his work. It shows in how he trains and get results. I am 65 years of age now and proud of how I look and feel. I met Curtis at the gym, he was a trainer there. I would still go to the gym and do a trekking and dance class. I missed Boot Camp so much that is why this year I just canceled my gym membership. I love working out outdoors. who wants to be enclosed? You are outdoors and hear the birds and see all the nature around you. In the six years I have know Curtis he is truly what he preaches. He is so into what he does and loves it. He greets us every morning with a smile. His workouts are difficult and he knows just how much he can push each of us to get the maximum results we want. The workouts are always different and not boring at all. He continually changes the workouts and the different equipment he uses. We all are pretty much addicted to the Boot Camp. I have met so many ladies and have become good friends. We encourage one another and help each other in any way we can. Last year February 1st, I started a treatment for my liver which went on for six months. Every Friday I had an injection in my stomach which was like chemo. I would feel sick and by Monday sometimes I did not want to work out, but still went. There were times when I would get out of breath just trying to run around the playground area and Curtis would still encourage me - keep going. This I do not forget. Especially since I had three personal trainers previously who did not compare to Curtis. With his encouragement I even did the stairs at Cal State Fullerton which is not easy when you are well. I did it at my own pace and was last to finish, but there was Curtis waiting for me with a high five. I finished my treatment last July and here I am strong as ever again with my liver fully healed. I encourage anyone to come and try the Boot Camp just for your health and the looks will be a plus. There are men who workout and walk around showing it all off. What I love about Curtis is that he has the great body with all the muscles and does not show it off or brag about it. He is so down to earth and really cares about the people he is training". Love,

text: "Boot Camp FX is a workout I can always be proud of and feel great from. If I work out on my own, I'm constantly battling mentally with trying to work harder than I feel like giving. Curtis mixes it up and makes it fun but challenging. I don't have to think about how hard it is. I just do whatever he says. With someone pushing me, I can give far more than I think I can on my own and I love that. I've also achieved tone and muscle mass I never really saw even after decades of working out. First and foremost, I'm a wife and mom to a great husband and 3 awesome kids. (That's my favorite job.) I'm also a graphic designer and an actress (that is, if I can book the job) and I sometimes write and produce scripts for the Children's Ministry at my church. I've always had a strong focus on sports and working out since elementary school. The fact that I've always been fairly fit, made it hard for me to think going to a boot camp was going to be worth my time and effort. But what I learned was that I was a Cardio Queen. I ran hard daily with no recovery days in between, which permanently messed up my knee. I never did full-body strength & cardio workouts. I did weights, but I always did the exact same weight exercises and not enough real weight to challenge my muscles. I could never figure out why my body never seemed to change with as hard as I believed I worked out. When I started seeing Curtis, I could handle what he threw at me because I was already in a pretty fit cardio state, but I started seeing definition all over that I never saw in years of working out. In addition, I now use boot camp as a daily goal to push myself harder and faster than I think I can go. I always leave boot camp feeling great. A friend I hadn't seen in a year or two was meeting me and another friend at a coffee house to hang out. Kristin walked into the coffee house and my jaw dropped. She looked awesome. She wasn't even flexing but her muscles were super defined, she was lean and toned, looking like a fitness model. I said, "What did you do? I want to look like you. You look amazing!" What's funny is that she looked great before the transformation. That fact that I even saw a difference was a definite "I want what you have" advertisement for Curtis' training. Boot camp was my first introduction to his killer fat burning exercises and it was fun getting pushed around. I started working out with another hard-core, butt-kicking boot camper named Nicole. She's become my favorite workout partner because she's encouraging but also such a hard worker that I am motivated to keep up with her high level of fitness. When you have people who can challenge you and make you encouraged to do more than you think you can do, you know you're in the right place. Muscle definition that was visible to me was the result that I initially saw, and that keeps me coming back for more. Now if I can just have more discipline in my eating, I might be able to look the way I want. In general, I'm a pretty happy person (spiritually, mentally and physically), but I definitely think that I get a huge mental boost after my boot camp fx workouts. My favorite feeling of accomplishment is when I go to a really hard boot camp that makes me feel like I want to pass out or throw up afterwards. I love that feeling of knowing I climbed a mountain I initially didn't think I could climb. I brought my friends Jaylene and Anita to boot camp. They love it. Jaylene still goes every day. All the women I work out with at the morning bootcamp are all motivated and have great attitudes. It makes for a fun, exciting atmosphere. I love working out with people who want to work hard. The newsletter: I always read the Fitness Cybernetics e-newsletter because it keeps my mind on the right track. It is not only a reminder to stay the course, but I value the information contained in it. Even if it's something I already know, the reminder solidifies it more completely in my mind. Boot camp: I appreciate that Curtis doesn't make everyone go at the exact same level all the time. Everyone does similar exercises, but if someone is more fit and can handle more, Curtis recognizes that and makes that person do something harder in order to fatigue more quickly. Someone asked me if Bootcamp was something I could replicate on my own and I answered that I didn't think I could fully replicate it on my own for several reasons. First, Curtis pushes me harder and further than I would push myself, and I appreciate that. When I ask Curtis if I can have a breather or stop for a second, he tells me "no, don't stop, go harder". Since I can't resist a challenge and I feel like he thinks there is more to squeeze out of me, I do what he tells me and I am prouder of accomplishing what I thought I didn't have the strength or energy to do. I know I couldn't do that to myself while working out alone. Secondly, I like not having to think about what exercise is coming next. If I'm going to utilize my strength and energy full force, the last thing I want to do is think. I'd rather get pushed around, being told what to do. Boot camp has also allowed me to stay dedicated and disciplined to both my fitness and nutrition in a way I've not been able to maintain on my own in the last 2 years since my baby was born. I'm not certain why that is, but perhaps it's because I'm accountable to someone else besides myself...and I'm also paying for the change to happen and I don't want to slack off because of it. I've dragged some friends with me to the Boot camp workouts and it's psychologically boosting for me to have my friends workout with me and being on the same nutrition plan. I don't feel alone in it, and we can all share our accomplishments together and encourage each other. Keep kicking my butt Curtis. I love it.

text: "Boot Camp FX is a workout I can always be proud of and feel great from. If I work out on my own, I'm constantly battling mentally with trying to work harder than I feel like giving. Curtis mixes it up and makes it fun but challenging. I don't have to think about how hard it is. I just do whatever he says. With someone pushing me, I can give far more than I think I can on my own and I love that. I've also achieved tone and muscle mass I never really saw even after decades of working out. First and foremost, I'm a wife and mom to a great husband and 3 awesome kids. (That's my favorite job.) I'm also a graphic designer and an actress (that is, if I can book the job) and I sometimes write and produce scripts for the Children's Ministry at my church. I've always had a strong focus on sports and working out since elementary school. The fact that I've always been fairly fit, made it hard for me to think going to a boot camp was going to be worth my time and effort. But what I learned was that I was a Cardio Queen. I ran hard daily with no recovery days in between, which permanently messed up my knee. I never did full-body strength & cardio workouts. I did weights, but I always did the exact same weight exercises and not enough real weight to challenge my muscles. I could never figure out why my body never seemed to change with as hard as I believed I worked out. When I started seeing Curtis, I could handle what he threw at me because I was already in a pretty fit cardio state, but I started seeing definition all over that I never saw in years of working out. In addition, I now use boot camp as a daily goal to push myself harder and faster than I think I can go. I always leave boot camp feeling great. A friend I hadn't seen in a year or two was meeting me and another friend at a coffee house to hang out. Kristin walked into the coffee house and my jaw dropped. She looked awesome. She wasn't even flexing but her muscles were super defined, she was lean and toned, looking like a fitness model. I said, "What did you do? I want to look like you. You look amazing!" What's funny is that she looked great before the transformation. That fact that I even saw a difference was a definite "I want what you have" advertisement for Curtis' training. Boot camp was my first introduction to his killer fat burning exercises and it was fun getting pushed around. I started working out with another hard-core, butt-kicking boot camper named Nicole. She's become my favorite workout partner because she's encouraging but also such a hard worker that I am motivated to keep up with her high level of fitness. When you have people who can challenge you and make you encouraged to do more than you think you can do, you know you're in the right place. Muscle definition that was visible to me was the result that I initially saw, and that keeps me coming back for more. Now if I can just have more discipline in my eating, I might be able to look the way I want. In general, I'm a pretty happy person (spiritually, mentally and physically), but I definitely think that I get a huge mental boost after my boot camp fx workouts. My favorite feeling of accomplishment is when I go to a really hard boot camp that makes me feel like I want to pass out or throw up afterwards. I love that feeling of knowing I climbed a mountain I initially didn't think I could climb. I brought my friends Jaylene and Anita to boot camp. They love it. Jaylene still goes every day. All the women I work out with at the morning bootcamp are all motivated and have great attitudes. It makes for a fun, exciting atmosphere. I love working out with people who want to work hard. The newsletter: I always read the Fitness Cybernetics e-newsletter because it keeps my mind on the right track. It is not only a reminder to stay the course, but I value the information contained in it. Even if it's something I already know, the reminder solidifies it more completely in my mind. Boot camp: I appreciate that Curtis doesn't make everyone go at the exact same level all the time. Everyone does similar exercises, but if someone is more fit and can handle more, Curtis recognizes that and makes that person do something harder in order to fatigue more quickly. Someone asked me if Bootcamp was something I could replicate on my own and I answered that I didn't think I could fully replicate it on my own for several reasons. First, Curtis pushes me harder and further than I would push myself, and I appreciate that. When I ask Curtis if I can have a breather or stop for a second, he tells me "no, don't stop, go harder". Since I can't resist a challenge and I feel like he thinks there is more to squeeze out of me, I do what he tells me and I am prouder of accomplishing what I thought I didn't have the strength or energy to do. I know I couldn't do that to myself while working out alone. Secondly, I like not having to think about what exercise is coming next. If I'm going to utilize my strength and energy full force, the last thing I want to do is think. I'd rather get pushed around, being told what to do. Boot camp has also allowed me to stay dedicated and disciplined to both my fitness and nutrition in a way I've not been able to maintain on my own in the last 2 years since my baby was born. I'm not certain why that is, but perhaps it's because I'm accountable to someone else besides myself...and I'm also paying for the change to happen and I don't want to slack off because of it. I've dragged some friends with me to the Boot camp workouts and it's psychologically boosting for me to have my friends workout with me and being on the same nutrition plan. I don't feel alone in it, and we can all share our accomplishments together and encourage each other. Keep kicking my butt Curtis. I love it.

text: "My business is property management. I manage my own houses and apartments. I have always worked out at a gym. This year I canceled my gym membership due to my loving Boot Camp so much. I work out at Boot Camp 5 days a week. My doctor's were so happy when I showed them results of my bone density test. My bone density was above average for my age. As we get older we lose muscle mass and that is why older people fall and break their bones much easier than a person who works out. I am 65 years young and besides having great bone density results from Boot Camp I am also more defined in area's where people my age have a lot of fat. Of course you also have to watch what you eat and Curtis has a great fat loss plan for you to follow and the fat does come off. In the past I have worked with four different trainers. As you know I am a cancer survivor or 6 Years now. I am a fighter and I give my all in everything in life. I appreciate so much more in life now and am grateful for everyday! I have to thank you for that changes that have taken place in my body. I have taken off more than 8 inches off my arms, hips, legs, and waist. I am so thankful Curtis did what four other trainers never did. This happened due to his dedication and love of his work. It shows in how he trains and get results. I am 65 years of age now and proud of how I look and feel. I met Curtis at the gym, he was a trainer there. I would still go to the gym and do a trekking and dance class. I missed Boot Camp so much that is why this year I just canceled my gym membership. I love working out outdoors. who wants to be enclosed? You are outdoors and hear the birds and see all the nature around you. In the six years I have know Curtis he is truly what he preaches. He is so into what he does and loves it. He greets us every morning with a smile. His workouts are difficult and he knows just how much he can push each of us to get the maximum results we want. The workouts are always different and not boring at all. He continually changes the workouts and the different equipment he uses. We all are pretty much addicted to the Boot Camp. I have met so many ladies and have become good friends. We encourage one another and help each other in any way we can. Last year February 1st, I started a treatment for my liver which went on for six months. Every Friday I had an injection in my stomach which was like chemo. I would feel sick and by Monday sometimes I did not want to work out, but still went. There were times when I would get out of breath just trying to run around the playground area and Curtis would still encourage me - keep going. This I do not forget. Especially since I had three personal trainers previously who did not compare to Curtis. With his encouragement I even did the stairs at Cal State Fullerton which is not easy when you are well. I did it at my own pace and was last to finish, but there was Curtis waiting for me with a high five. I finished my treatment last July and here I am strong as ever again with my liver fully healed. I encourage anyone to come and try the Boot Camp just for your health and the looks will be a plus. There are men who workout and walk around showing it all off. What I love about Curtis is that he has the great body with all the muscles and does not show it off or brag about it. He is so down to earth and really cares about the people he is training". Love,

text: "First of all, I have had trainers in the past, however, I find that the result is quite different. My experience with previous trainers was a definite change in my body tone, balance and motivation, but that's where it stopped. I find that the difference with Boot Camp FX is that I have gained stamina. Prior to Boot Camp FX my personal routine was Pilates a few times a week and jog 2 miles on Saturday. On my 2 miles I would start out jogging, but before I got to the first mile I had to take walking breaks. Last weekend I jogged 4 miles non stop. I did a lot of sweating, but my breathing was never labored and my legs didn't get sore at all. Boot Camp FX has certainly given me tone, balance and motivation just as the other trainers did, but without the endurance factor you don't realize your TRUE POTENTIAL. This is good stuff". Curtis, I have never been a runner. Never trained for anything like this, but "I JUST RAN THE 2010 LA MARATHON....ALL 26.2 MILES" I took your class starting August 3rd thru October 31st of 2009. I must admit that this was the kick start of my training for the Marathon. In your class, you take people beyond their expectations of what their bodies can do. The element of surprise of never knowing what you will be doing and what feat you will accomplish that day is what keeps people motivated. It's hard to get up at 5 a.m. to arrive at the park in the dark to work out, but if you miss a day, you just don't feel right. You wonder what you have missed. At age 51, I must say that I never would have imagined running a full Marathon, completing it, without injury, in 5 hours 41 minutes. No kidding....my time is still posted (bib #15262). THANK YOU CURTIS.....for giving me the stamina and drive. God Bless,

text: Before meeting Curtis, I had always been an active person, but I was also definitely someone who had a hard time fighting the temptation of the quick-fix if I was unsettled with results (i.e. diet pills/crazes of the moment). I had never been able to find a healthy balance or a body I was happy with. I needed to change, not only for my wedding gown at the time I started, but also for my health and for the loved ones around me who were also directly affected by my moodiness, when I constantly felt like I had failed. Being the girl who has tried everything, I can honestly say that there is no one or anything better than Curtis Ludlow & Bootcamp FX. While knowing the right times to push and always challenging me & other campers to reach beyond our goals in a positive way, the constant support and passion for his craft carries us through.
